16 December 2026

Monetary Policy Report

Monetary Policy Report, December 2026.

Summary

CPIF inflation is expected to rise to 2.0 per cent in 2026 and average 1.9 per cent in 2027. GDP is expected to grow by 2.1 per cent in 2026.

Monetary policy in Sweden — the Riksbank's strategy

Monetary policy in Sweden is contractionary, aimed at bringing inflation back to the target of 2 per cent. The Executive Board decided to cut the policy rate by 0.25 percentage points to 2.5 per cent.

The economic outlook for the coming years

Economic activity is gradually strengthening.

The labour market

Unemployment is expected to be 7.2 per cent in 2026. Wage growth is expected to be 3.3 per cent in 2026.

Inflation

Inflation has fallen markedly from the peak. Underlying inflation, CPIF excluding energy, is expected to be 2.3 per cent in 2026.

Financial conditions

Financial conditions have eased somewhat in recent months.

Monetary policy analysis

The policy rate can also be cut or lowered further if inflation remains low. Monetary policy needs to remain contractionary for some time to come.

Uncertainty, risks and alternative scenarios

The risks surrounding the inflation outlook are assessed to be broadly balanced. Risks to economic activity are tilted to the downside.
